title: Judges Chapter 10 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Judges chapter 10 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Judges Chapter 10 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Judges Chapter 10.

questions.question: Who arose to defend Israel after Abimelech?
questions.correctAnswer: Tola
questions.explanation: Judges 10:1 states that after Abimelech, Tola the son of Puah arose to defend Israel.

questions.question: How many years did Tola judge Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: 23 years
questions.explanation: Judges 10:2 says Tola judged Israel for twenty and three years.

questions.question: Where was Tola buried?
questions.correctAnswer: Shamir
questions.explanation: Judges 10:2 records that Tola was buried in Shamir.

questions.question: Who judged Israel after Tola?
questions.correctAnswer: Jair
questions.explanation: Judges 10:3 states that after Tola, Jair, a Gileadite, judged Israel.

questions.question: For how many years did Jair judge Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: 22 years
questions.explanation: Judges 10:3 says Jair judged Israel for twenty and two years.

questions.question: How many sons did Jair have who rode on ass colts?
questions.explanation: Judges 10:4 records that Jair had thirty sons who rode on thirty ass colts.

questions.question: What are the thirty cities associated with Jair's sons called?
questions.correctAnswer: Havothjair
questions.explanation: Judges 10:4 states the thirty cities are called Havothjair unto this day.

questions.question: Where was Jair buried?
questions.correctAnswer: Camon
questions.explanation: Judges 10:5 says Jair died and was buried in Camon.

questions.question: Which gods did the children of Israel serve when they did evil again?
options: Baalim, Ashtaroth, and the gods of Syria
questions.correctAnswer: Baalim, Ashtaroth, and the gods of Syria
questions.explanation: Judges 10:6 lists Baalim, Ashtaroth, and the gods of Syria among those served by Israel.

questions.question: True or False: Tola was a man of the tribe of Issachar.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 10:1 identifies Tola as a man of Issachar.

questions.question: True or False: Jair had twenty sons who ruled thirty cities.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 10:4 states Jair had thirty sons that had thirty cities, not twenty sons.

questions.question: True or False: The anger of the LORD was hot against Israel because they served the LORD faithfully.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 10:7 shows that the LORD's anger was because Israel did evil and served other gods, not Him.

questions.question: True or False: The children of Israel served not the LORD but other gods.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 10:6 clearly states that Israel forsook the LORD and served not Him.

questions.question: What city did Jair's sons' thirty cities lie in?
questions.correctAnswer: Gilead
questions.explanation: Judges 10:4 declares the thirty cities called Havothjair are in the land of Gilead.

questions.question: In Judges 10, which event happened first?
options: Jair died and was buried in Camon
questions.correctAnswer: Tola judged Israel
questions.explanation: Judges 10:1-2 shows Tola judged Israel before Jair (Judges 10:3).

medium.title: Judges Chapter 10 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Judges Chapter 10 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who did the Lord sell Israel into the hands of because of their evil?
options: The Philistines and the children of Ammon
questions.correctAnswer: The Philistines and the children of Ammon
questions.explanation: Judges 10:7 states that the LORD was angry and sold Israel into the hands of the Philistines and the children of Ammon due to their evil deeds. This connects to their disobedience in Judges 10:6.

questions.question: For how many years did the Philistines and children of Ammon oppress Israel on the other side Jordan?
questions.correctAnswer: 18 years
questions.explanation: Judges 10:8 clearly states that Israel was vexed and oppressed for eighteen years on the other side Jordan in the land of the Amorites, linking their punishment to their previous disobedience.

questions.question: Which tribes did the children of Ammon fight against besides those on the other side Jordan?
options: Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim
questions.correctAnswer: Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim
questions.explanation: Judges 10:9 tells us that the children of Ammon passed over Jordan to fight against Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim, causing great distress to Israel.

questions.question: According to Judges 10:10, what did the children of Israel admit when they cried unto the LORD?
options: They had sinned by forsaking God and serving Baalim
They were innocent and sought justice
They had served only the LORD faithfully
They wanted to build altars for new gods
questions.correctAnswer: They had sinned by forsaking God and serving Baalim
questions.explanation: Judges 10:10 reveals Israel's confession of sinfulness for forsaking God and serving Baalim, showing their recognition of wrongdoing and need for repentance.

questions.question: How does Judges 10:11 remind Israel of God's past deliverance?
options: By listing deliverance from Egyptians, Amorites, children of Ammon, and Philistines
By mentioning the creation of the world
By recalling the giving of the Ten Commandments
By recounting the flood in Noah's time
questions.correctAnswer: By listing deliverance from Egyptians, Amorites, children of Ammon, and Philistines
questions.explanation: In Judges 10:11, the LORD asks Israel if He did not deliver them from the Egyptians, Amorites, children of Ammon, and Philistines, reminding them of His faithfulness in past deliverances.

questions.question: Which additional groups oppressed Israel, as mentioned in Judges 10:12, and from whom did God deliver them when they cried out?
questions.correctAnswer: Zidonians, Amalekites, and Maonites
questions.explanation: Judges 10:12 states these groups oppressed Israel, and when Israel cried out, God delivered them, demonstrating His mercy despite their repeated disobedience.

questions.question: What was God's response to Israel's repeated forsaking of Him to serve other gods, according to Judges 10:13?
options: He declared He would no longer deliver them
He promised to send a prophet
He commanded them to build an altar
questions.correctAnswer: He declared He would no longer deliver them
questions.explanation: Judges 10:13 shows God's righteous judgment because Israel forsook Him and served other gods; He stated He would deliver them no more, emphasizing consequences for unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What challenge did God give Israel in Judges 10:14 after He said He would not deliver them?
options: To cry to the gods they had chosen to see if they would deliver them
To build a temple for the LORD
To fast and pray for 40 days
questions.correctAnswer: To cry to the gods they had chosen to see if they would deliver them
questions.explanation: In Judges 10:14, God challenges Israel to cry to the gods they had chosen, highlighting the futility of false gods compared to the LORD's power and faithfulness.

questions.question: How did Israel respond to God's challenge in Judges 10:15?
options: They confessed their sin and pleaded for deliverance
They rejected God and worshiped idols more
They asked for a new king
questions.correctAnswer: They confessed their sin and pleaded for deliverance
questions.explanation: Judges 10:15 records Israel's humble confession and plea for God's mercy, demonstrating repentance and faith despite previous disobedience.

questions.question: What change did Israel make according to Judges 10:16 after confessing their sin?
options: They put away strange gods and served the LORD
They built more altars for Baalim
They fled the land of Gilead
They continued to serve other gods secretly
questions.correctAnswer: They put away strange gods and served the LORD
questions.explanation: Judges 10:16 shows Israel's repentance through removing foreign gods and returning to serve the LORD, which grieved God's soul for their misery, indicating His compassion.

questions.question: True or False: According to Judges 10:17, the children of Ammon gathered and encamped in Mizpeh.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 10:17 states that the children of Ammon encamped in Gilead, while the children of Israel assembled in Mizpeh, showing the distinction between their camps.

questions.question: Who was to be made the head over all the inhabitants of Gilead if he began to fight against the children of Ammon, as per Judges 10:18?
options: The man who will first begin the fight against the children of Ammon
The judge appointed by the elders
questions.correctAnswer: The man who will first begin the fight against the children of Ammon
questions.explanation: Judges 10:18 records the people and princes of Gilead agreeing that whoever starts the fight against Ammon shall be made head over all Gilead, emphasizing leadership through courage.

questions.question: How does the passage in Judges 10:10-12 teach about the importance of humility and repentance?
options: It shows Israel confessed their sins and God reminded them of past deliverances
It encourages ignoring consequences for sin
It teaches that God will always deliver regardless of attitudes
It advises to serve multiple gods for protection
questions.correctAnswer: It shows Israel confessed their sins and God reminded them of past deliverances
questions.explanation: Judges 10:10-12 illustrate Israel’s humble confession of sin and God's reminder of His faithful deliverance, teaching that repentance and humility open the door to God's mercy.

questions.question: What does Judges 10:13-14 suggest will happen if Israel continues in idolatry instead of returning to God?
options: God will no longer deliver them and they must rely on their chosen gods
God will send immediate punishment without warning
God will send another judge automatically
questions.correctAnswer: God will no longer deliver them and they must rely on their chosen gods
questions.explanation: Judges 10:13-14 warn that continued idolatry will result in God withholding deliverance, forcing Israel to depend on false gods they have chosen, highlighting the consequences of disobedience.

questions.question: True or False: Judges 10:16 shows that God was indifferent to the misery of Israel after they put away strange gods.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 10:16 states that God's soul was grieved for the misery of Israel even after they repented, showing His compassion and concern, not indifference.

hard.title: Judges Chapter 10 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Judges Chapter 10.

questions.question: What reason does the LORD give for refusing to deliver Israel again according to Judges 10?
options: Because they have forsaken Him and served other gods
Because they did not pray sincerely
Because they refused to gather at Mizpeh
questions.correctAnswer: Because they have forsaken Him and served other gods
questions.explanation: Judges 10:13 states that Israel had forsaken the LORD and served other gods, and therefore He would deliver them no more.

questions.question: According to Judges 10, what does the LORD tell Israel to do after declaring He will deliver them no more?
options: Cry unto the gods they have chosen to deliver them
Gather at Mizpeh and prepare for battle
questions.correctAnswer: Cry unto the gods they have chosen to deliver them
questions.explanation: In Judges 10:14, the LORD tells Israel to cry to the gods they have chosen and let them deliver them in their tribulation.

questions.question: What is Israel's response after the LORD refuses to deliver them in Judges 10?
options: They confess their sin and ask the LORD to do whatever seems good to Him
They continue to worship the gods of the Ammonites
They seek help from the Philistines
They appoint a new judge immediately
questions.correctAnswer: They confess their sin and ask the LORD to do whatever seems good to Him
questions.explanation: Judges 10:15 records Israel's confession of sin and their plea for deliverance according to the LORD's will.

questions.question: What action do the children of Israel take after confessing their sins in Judges 10?
options: They put away strange gods and served the LORD
They built high places for Baalim
They made a covenant with Ammon
questions.correctAnswer: They put away strange gods and served the LORD
questions.explanation: Judges 10:16 explains that Israel removed the strange gods and served the LORD, which grieved His soul for their misery.

questions.question: Where did the children of Ammon encamp as they prepared for battle against Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Gilead
questions.explanation: Judges 10:17 states that the children of Ammon gathered and encamped in Gilead.

questions.question: Where did the children of Israel assemble themselves to confront the children of Ammon?
questions.correctAnswer: Mizpeh
questions.explanation: Judges 10:17 records that Israel assembled and encamped in Mizpeh to face the children of Ammon.

questions.question: What title was given to the man who would lead the fight against the children of Ammon according to the princes of Gilead?
options: Head over all the inhabitants of Gilead
questions.correctAnswer: Head over all the inhabitants of Gilead
questions.explanation: Judges 10:18 shows the princes of Gilead declaring that the man who begins to fight against Ammon would be head over all inhabitants of Gilead.

questions.question: The word 'forsaken' as used in Judges 10:13 (Hebrew root עָזַב, azab) primarily means:
questions.correctAnswer: To abandon or leave entirely
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word עָזַב (azab) means to forsake or abandon completely, as Israel did by leaving the LORD to serve other gods (Judges 10:13).

questions.question: Which earlier Old Testament event does the LORD reference in Judges 10:11 to remind Israel of His deliverance?
questions.correctAnswer: Deliverance from the Egyptians
questions.explanation: Judges 10:11 recalls how the LORD delivered Israel from the Egyptians, along with other oppressors, reminding them of His past faithfulness.

questions.question: The theme of Israel's repeated cycle of sin and deliverance in Judges 10 reflects which broader literary device found throughout the book?
questions.correctAnswer: Cycle of Apostasy and Redemption
questions.explanation: The cycle of Israel sinning, being oppressed, crying to God, and being delivered is a key literary and theological pattern running through Judges, including chapter 10.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of Israel's confession and repentance found in Judges 10:15-16?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Chronicles 7:14
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 7:14 similarly records Israel's confession and repentance as the condition for God's healing and forgiveness, paralleling Judges 10:15-16.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD's soul being grieved in Judges 10:16 indicates a personal, emotional response to Israel's suffering.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 10:16 shows the LORD's soul was grieved for Israel's misery, indicating a personal and emotional involvement in their plight.

questions.question: True or False: According to Judges 10:7-8, Israel was oppressed only by the Philistines after serving other gods.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 10:7-8 explains Israel was sold into the hands of both the Philistines and the children of Ammon, indicating multiple oppressors.

questions.question: Which other book of the Bible contains a similar account of Israel serving foreign gods and being delivered when they repent, paralleling Judges 10?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Kings
questions.explanation: 1 Kings chapters 11-12 describe Israel's turning to foreign gods and subsequent judgment, paralleling the cycle in Judges 10.

questions.question: The thirty sons of Jair each riding on thirty ass colts symbolically suggest:
options: A display of wealth and political influence in Gilead
questions.correctAnswer: A display of wealth and political influence in Gilead
questions.explanation: Judges 10:4 indicates Jair's sons rode on thirty ass colts and had thirty cities, symbolizing their status and power in the land of Gilead.

theological.title: Judges Chapter 10 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Judges Chapter 10 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily revealed when the LORD refuses to deliver Israel because they served other gods, as stated in Judges 10:13?
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice
questions.explanation: Judges 10:13 shows that God will no longer deliver Israel because they forsook Him and served other gods, highlighting His attribute of justice in punishing sin.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by Israel's repeated cycle of sin, oppression, repentance, and deliverance as seen in Judges 10:6-16?
options: The doctrine of human depravity and divine redemption
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of human depravity and divine redemption
questions.explanation: Judges 10:6-16 shows Israel's continual evil and idolatry followed by their repentance and God's willingness to forgive and deliver, illustrating human sinfulness and God's redeeming grace.

questions.question: Who is described as having thirty sons who rode on thirty ass colts and possessed thirty cities in Judges 10:4?
questions.correctAnswer: Jair
questions.explanation: Judges 10:4 describes Jair as having thirty sons who rode on thirty ass colts and controlled thirty cities in Gilead.

questions.question: According to Judges 10:8, how long did the Philistines and children of Ammon oppress Israel on the east side of the Jordan?
questions.correctAnswer: Eighteen years
questions.explanation: Judges 10:8 states that Israel was vexed and oppressed for eighteen years by the Philistines and children of Ammon in Gilead.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth emerges from Judges 10:10 and Judges 10:15 about Israel's attitude toward sin and God's response?
options: True repentance involves confession and surrender to God's will
questions.correctAnswer: True repentance involves confession and surrender to God's will
questions.explanation: Judges 10:10 shows Israel confessing their sin, and 10:15 shows them submitting to God's judgment while pleading for deliverance, illustrating authentic repentance.

questions.question: What does Judges 10:16 reveal about God's nature when it says His soul was grieved for the misery of Israel?
options: God is impassible and unaffected by human suffering
God is indifferent to human sin
God is compassionate and emotionally engaged with His people
God is withdrawn during times of judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God is compassionate and emotionally engaged with His people
questions.explanation: Judges 10:16 shows God's grief over Israel’s misery, revealing His compassionate nature and emotional involvement with His covenant people.

questions.question: How does Judges 10:11-12 demonstrate God's faithfulness in the covenantal relationship with Israel despite their sin?
options: God repeatedly delivers Israel when they repent
God punishes Israel without any deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: God repeatedly delivers Israel when they repent
questions.explanation: Judges 10:11-12 recount God's past deliverances of Israel from various enemies, showing His faithfulness despite their repeated sins.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's anger and punishment in Judges 10 show Him as cruel and unforgiving. What does Judges 10:6-16 actually teach about God's character in response to Israel's sin and repentance?
options: God is unchangingly wrathful without mercy
God punishes sin but remains open to repentance and shows mercy
God ignores sin and never disciplines His people
God's punishment is arbitrary and unrelated to sin
questions.correctAnswer: God punishes sin but remains open to repentance and shows mercy
questions.explanation: Judges 10:6-16 reveals God's righteous anger against sin but also His willingness to forgive and relieve suffering when Israel sincerely repents, demonstrating both justice and mercy.

questions.question: What does the narrative arc from Judges 10:1-5 demonstrate about the role of judges in Israel’s history?
options: Judges were permanent kings of Israel
Judges were military deliverers and spiritual governors during times of crisis
Judges were foreign rulers imposed on Israel
Judges had no influence on Israel's spiritual life
questions.correctAnswer: Judges were military deliverers and spiritual governors during times of crisis
questions.explanation: Judges 10:1-5 introduces Tola and Jair as judges who led Israel for many years, indicating their role as leaders who defended and judged Israel in turbulent times.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Judges 10:14 when He challenges Israel to cry to their chosen gods during tribulation?
options: God's sovereignty and supremacy over false gods
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty and supremacy over false gods
questions.explanation: Judges 10:14 displays God's sovereign challenge to Israel's idols, emphasizing His supremacy over all so-called gods.

questions.question: How do Judges 10:17-18 contribute to the theological understanding of leadership and community responsibility in times of national crisis?
options: Leadership is unimportant in times of war
Community leaders seek and appoint a head to lead in battle, showing collective responsibility
Only one individual should decide for the nation
questions.correctAnswer: Community leaders seek and appoint a head to lead in battle, showing collective responsibility
questions.explanation: Judges 10:17-18 describes the princes of Gilead consulting and appointing a leader to fight Ammon, illustrating shared leadership responsibility during crisis.

questions.question: What combined theological insight is gained from Judges 10:7 and 10:9 about the consequences of Israel's apostasy?
options: Israel's apostasy led to peace and prosperity
Israel's apostasy resulted in God's anger, oppression by enemies, and widespread distress
Israel was unaffected by their sin
Israel's enemies were powerless against them
questions.correctAnswer: Israel's apostasy resulted in God's anger, oppression by enemies, and widespread distress
questions.explanation: Judges 10:7 shows God's anger and handing Israel over to enemies, and 10:9 describes the distress caused by multiple enemies attacking Israel due to their sin.

questions.question: Which doctrinal truth concerning idolatry is taught in Judges 10:6 about Israel's spiritual failure?
options: Idolatry was a minor issue for Israel
Idolatry involved serving multiple foreign gods and abandoning the LORD
Idolatry was encouraged by the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry involved serving multiple foreign gods and abandoning the LORD
questions.explanation: Judges 10:6 explains that Israel served Baalim, Ashtaroth, and gods of surrounding nations, forsaking the LORD, showing the depth of their idolatry.

questions.question: What does Judges 10:2 teach about the temporality of human leadership compared to God's enduring covenant?
options: Human judges reign eternally like God
Human judges have limited lifespans and authority, unlike God's eternal covenant
God's covenant depends on human leaders
questions.correctAnswer: Human judges have limited lifespans and authority, unlike God's eternal covenant
questions.explanation: Judges 10:2 mentions Tola judged Israel for 23 years and then died, highlighting the temporary nature of human leadership vs. God's eternal faithfulness.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is reflected in Judges 10:15 when Israel submits to God's will and pleads for deliverance despite their sin?
options: The doctrine of divine sovereignty and human submission
The doctrine of predestination without human response
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine sovereignty and human submission
questions.explanation: Judges 10:15 shows Israel acknowledging God's authority to do as He sees fit and appealing to His mercy, reflecting submission to divine sovereignty.
